extracted.intended_audience: news publishers and site owners using Google News / Publisher Center
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for news publishers about the algorithmic factors and policies that influence how content is ranked and personalized within Google News and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the main algorithmic factors that influence ranking in Google News. (Page does not provide further detail here; links point to more information about how stories are selected.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a ranking factor—meant to capture how prominently a topic or source is recognized or cited. No detailed breakdown on this page; consult linked materials for examples and signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritativeness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a core factor affecting ranking, indicating the weight given to perceived trustworthiness/expertise of source or content. Page itself does not enumerate specific signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a ranking factor, reflecting recency of content. Particularly relevant for news contexts where timeliness matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called out as an influence on ranking; implies site and content should be usable (e.g., load/performance, mobile-friendliness, ad experience), though specific usability criteria are not listed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranking is influenced by geographic location and language; helps serve locally relevant content to users in appropriate languages/regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization (user interests and activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms may personalize your news based on certain factors, including your interests, either that you’ve specified or that we inferred from your past activity on Google products and Youtube, depending on your activity settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes algorithms may personalize content for specific sections ('For you' in Home; Topics, sources, and locations in Following; 'Picks for you' in briefing). Personalization depends on user-specified interests or inferred behavior from Google products and YouTube, subject to activity settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments and advertising programs do not affect ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Google News aims to promote original journalism and expose users to diverse perspectives. It doesn't accept payments to expedite or improve a site’s search appearance or ranking. Participation in an advertising program like AdSense has no effect on ranking of your site in Google News, or on any other Google search engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy assurance that paid arrangements and participation in advertising programs do not influence Google News ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a Google-friendly website
rubrics_metrics.description: You can improve your site's ranking by maintaining a Google-friendly website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page links to guidance on how Google ranks pages in Search and how to make sites Google-friendly; implies following general Search quality and technical best practices (site structure, indexing, speed, mobile-friendliness, etc.) can help news ranking.
